tytul: Pickled knight mushrooms: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for yellow knight (Tricholoma equestre, Polish gąska zielona) and grey knight (gąska siwa) mushrooms pickled in vinegar.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Drying and cooking do not destroy the toxins of poisonous mushrooms, and only an expert can tell edible species from poisonous ones.

In 2003 the French food safety agency (Afssa) found that no safe intake dose of the yellow knight mushroom (Tricholoma equestre, Polish gąska zielona) can be established on scientific grounds, and recommended considering measures so that it is no longer offered for consumption in any form.

akapity: NCHFP warns: do not can wild mushrooms; its tested canning process is only for small to medium-size cultivated mushrooms with unopened caps.
JarAtlas treats mushrooms pickled in vinegar and processed in jars in a boiling-water bath as canned mushrooms, so it applies this warning to them too.
The FDA list gives mushrooms a pH of about 6.00–6.70, while acid foods are foods with a natural pH of 4.6 or lower.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for wild mushrooms in vinegar from a checked source.
